diagnostic:
Revision round: only the development-only store fault refuse_mark_repo_read_after_first and its L6 cases. The resume and count behaviour was not touched.

What was built. ScanWriteFault gains RefuseMarkRepoReadAfterFirst (cfg(debug_assertions) only; the release twin still has no values). ScanWrite is now ScanWrite<'a> and its MarkRepoRead member carries the run id the store already holds at that call site (crates/adapter-review-store/src/scan_runs.rs mark_repo_read). The new ScanWriteSeam owns the fault AND the runs that already saved a mark, so neither can be set without the other; the store holds it as Mutex<ScanWriteSeam> and admits_scan_write is the one effect-shell site that reads and updates it under that lock. The decision stays pure and total: admits(fault, write, saved_a_mark) -> Result<(), StoreError>, one arm per fault, the after-first arm refusing only when that run already saved a mark. The seam remembers a run only while a fault is held, so a production store carries no seam state (design: "a development-only seam adds no production state"). config.rs parses the one new name in the cfg(debug_assertions) parser and its property table gains the row; wiring.rs maps the name to the new store fault; the xtask token list gains both spellings and the guard test gains a gated and an ungated case for the new name.

L6 tests (the two declared cases), in the store adapter's own in-crate tests, crates/adapter-review-store/src/scan_runs.rs: a_run_saves_its_first_mark_and_is_refused_the_next (first mark saved, next refused naming the test fault, refused row stays planned, the run accounts for one read) and the_run_after_it_saves_its_own_first_mark (the next run's first mark saved again, its next refused, plan write and account-checks write of both runs admitted, the latest run accounts for the whole scan so far). They open the store through a new pub(crate) ReviewStore::in_memory_with(key, faults); open_in_memory now delegates to it. No oracle, support or feature record was touched.

GREEN on this Mac host: cargo test -p review-domain -p adapter-review-store exit 0 (adapter unit 49 passed 0 failed, +2 new; migration_v1_to_v2 6 passed; review-domain 105 + 28 + 34 + 2 passed). cargo xtask check-arch exit 0 ("check-arch: OK (30 workspace members)"). cargo test -p xtask --test review_app_test_fault_guard exit 0, 7 passed 0 failed (5 before). cargo test -p openlore-review-app --bins exit 0, 39 passed 0 failed. cargo clippy -p review-domain -p ports -p adapter-review-store -p openlore-review-app -p xtask --all-targets exit 0, no warning. cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_repos_read_across_resume exit 0, 10 passed 0 failed (the queue still reads "3 repos read"). cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_scan_store_failure exit 0, 4 passed 0 failed.

Design command deviation, no behaviour hidden: command 6 of the design reads "cargo test -p openlore-review-app --lib" and exits 101 with "no library targets found in package openlore-review-app" - that crate is a binary composition root. Its equivalent in-crate suite, cargo test -p openlore-review-app --bins, was run and is green; both are recorded with their real exits. Design owns the command text.

Mutation probe, serial, scoped to the changed lines (cargo mutants -p adapter-review-store -f crates/adapter-review-store/src/lib.rs -f crates/adapter-review-store/src/scan_runs.rs --in-diff feature.diff -j 1 --timeout 180, exit 2 = a missed mutant): 13 mutants, 8 caught, 1 missed, 4 unviable, baseline ok. Kill rate over viable mutants 8/9 = 88.9%, above the 80% gate. The one missed mutant deletes the match arm of the two PRE-EXISTING faults (RefuseMarkRepoRead, RefuseRecordAccountChecks); no adapter-package test observes it, and whether the acceptance suite review_app_scan_store_failure kills it was not measured in this probe, whose test scope was the adapter package only. Nothing of the new after-first arm is missed: its arm deletion, admits, answer, saved_a_mark (both replacements), remember, admits_scan_write and mark_repo_read were all caught. feature.diff was removed afterwards; no proptest regression file was produced; nothing was committed.

typesafe: unavailable - jev_decide.py exit 3, TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent from the shell environment of this host, so the one open choice (whether the seam remembers an admitted mark when no fault is held) was settled locally against the authority text "a development-only seam adds no production state".
